rv.q: At the beginning of Chicago writer Erik Gernand’s drama Year One , small-town doctor Anna delivers a monologue about helping a patient with appendicitis onto the table. The man asks her, “Are you one of them? I won’t let some vermin touch me.”
Smartly directed by Enrico Spada , Year One uses historical events as an allegory for our current political climate.
The cast of five is quite capable with strong performances by Pavlovich and Copeland as the young couple.

But an allegory dedicated to a moral message wherein a looming villain never appears leaves Gernand's characters flat and insubstantial compared to the size of the portentous evil always overshadowing them.
There's a wishy-washiness to 'Year One' that saps its impact.
